title_original: The Inner Images of Fashion Designer Marina Yee
excerpt_original: A year after her death, a book and a Belgian exhibition open up the secret world of Marina Yee, artist and member of the Antwerp Six. L’article The Inner Images of Fashion Designer Marina Yee est apparu en premier sur Blind Magazine .

blocks.text: A year after her death, a book and a Belgian exhibition open up the secret world of Marina Yee, artist and member of the Antwerp Six.
By Guénola Pellen. Photos by Marina Yee. Portrait by Alex Conu .

Few designers have counted for so much in fashion while showing themselves so little. Marina Yee studied at Antwerp’s Royal Academy of Fine Arts in the late 1970s, alongside the future Antwerp Six, who would overturn the silhouette of the 1980s. The city’s experimental scene held her closer, heir to Fluxus, which dissolved art into ordinary life, and to the Provos, Amsterdam’s insolent anarchists. She “was interested in other art forms too,” writes Chris Dercon, director of the Fondation Cartier.

Her label Marie started in 1986 and stopped a few seasons later, the pace of fashion suiting her badly. “I live and work like a loner or a hermit,” she said of her studio. There she stacked jars of iron and boxes of broken glass, the salvage she calls damaged goods. In 2010, she drowned her own face in black paint, on photographs where a single blonde strand gives her away.

Her comeback began in 2017, reached the Laila store in Tokyo the following year, then took the name M.Y. Collection in 2021, with Rafael Adriaensens. “I finally get recognition,” she said. On October 23, 2025, she spoke about her work at length for the first time, to the gallerist Sofie Van de Velde. Her assemblages hold together with tape: “You would have to take photographs of them to keep them.” Marina Yee died of cancer nine days later, at 67.

On March 28, 2026, MoMu, Antwerp’s fashion museum, opened “The Antwerp Six,” a retrospective of the collective. With the curator Geert Bruloot, Marina Yee had decided to replay her studio there. They had the interior photographed in minute detail, papered the walls of a scale model with the prints, then set the real objects back in front of them. Two windows open onto the scene, where some twenty centimeters separate things from their image. Curator Romy Cockx calls it “a carefully composed landscape of memories, finds and possibilities.”

The book shuffles her sketches, her photographic collages and her handwritten notes, in no order at all. Chris Dercon and Kaat Debo, director of MoMu, supply the texts. “This book is a glimpse into the mindset of Marina,” the closing page reads, “it is about finding beauty in the chaos.”

The exhibition “Marina Yee – Dreamscapes” runs at Gallery Sofie Van de Velde in Antwerp (Belgium), from November 28, 2026 to January 3, 2027. “The Antwerp Six” remains on view at MoMu until January 17, 2027. The book Marina Yee , 272 pages, is published by Hannibal Books, and will be available on November 28, 2026 at €69.
